blocks.text: Mnemonic: HEAD – HANDS – SITTING – STANDING – WALKING – TALKING

blocks.title: Developmental milestones are age-specific skills acquired by children in four major domains:

rows: Rolls over and sits with support
Runs stiffly and climbs onto furniture
Runs well and walks up stairs with assistance
Pedals tricycle and climbs stairs alternating feet

blocks.text: Mnemonic: REACH – GRASP – TRANSFER – PINCER – DRAW

rows: Builds a tower of approximately 6 blocks
Copies a square and draws a person with several body parts

blocks.text: Mnemonic: COO – BABBLE – MAMA – WORDS – PHRASES – SENTENCES

rows: Uses longer sentences and tells simple stories
Speaks in complex sentences and can recount events

blocks.text: Mnemonic: SMILE – RECOGNISE – PLAY – SHARE – INTERACT

rows: Waves bye-bye and plays simple interactive games

items.text: 6 months: Sits with support and transfers objects.
9 months: Sits independently and develops stranger anxiety.
12 months: Stands or cruises and uses meaningful words.
2 years: Runs and combines two words.
5 years: Skips and draws more complex shapes.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Developmental milestones have normal variation. Use the child's overall developmental profile rather than relying on one milestone in isolation.
Developmental delay means failure to achieve expected developmental milestones at the appropriate age.

rows: Down syndrome and other chromosomal disorders
Significant delay in at least two developmental domains in a child under 5 years

items.text: No social smile by around 3 months.
No two-word spontaneous phrases by 24 months.
Any loss of previously acquired skills.

blocks.text: These are screening warning signs rather than absolute diagnostic cut-offs.
Exam pearl: Developmental regression is particularly concerning and requires urgent evaluation for neurological, metabolic and neurodegenerative disorders.
Failure to thrive describes inadequate weight gain or growth in a child, usually assessed using serial growth measurements.
Exam pearl: A child who is failing to gain weight may initially have normal length and head circumference. Serial measurements are more informative than a single weight.
Short stature is generally defined as height below −2 standard deviations (SD) for age and sex, approximately below the 2nd–3rd percentile.

rows: Restricted growth (intrauterine growth restriction and malnutrition)

items.text: Bone age usually appropriate for chronological age.

blocks.text: 2. Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

items.text: Often a family history of late puberty.

rows: Often family history of delayed puberty
Puberty usually occurs at normal age

blocks.text: Exam pearl: A child with falling height percentiles or reduced growth velocity requires investigation even if their height has not yet fallen below −2 SD.
Tall stature is generally defined as height above +2 SD for age and sex.

rows: Advanced growth due to hormonal excess

items.text: Precocious puberty, which can cause early accelerated growth but may lead to reduced final adult height.

rows: Long limbs, arachnodactyly, lens dislocation, aortic root dilatation
Tall stature, small testes, hypogonadism, infertility
Excessive childhood growth, macrocephaly, developmental delay
Excess growth hormone before epiphyseal closure

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Tall stature with disproportionate long limbs, joint laxity and cardiovascular abnormalities should raise suspicion of Marfan syndrome.
Microcephaly is a head circumference below −2 SD for age and sex, usually below the 3rd percentile.

rows: Low maternal nutrition and placental insufficiency

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Always measure head circumference accurately and compare it with age- and sex-specific growth charts. A small head alone does not establish neurological impairment.
Macrocephaly is a head circumference above +2 SD for age and sex, usually above the 97th percentile.

rows: Excess CSF accumulation with ventricular enlargement

blocks.text: Clinical features suggesting raised intracranial pressure
Exam pearl: A rapidly increasing head circumference crossing multiple centile lines is more concerning than a stable large head that follows a consistent growth trajectory.

items.text: No pointing or gestures by around 12 months.
No meaningful single words by 16 months.
No spontaneous two-word phrases by 24 months.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Hearing impairment must be excluded in every child with unexplained delayed speech, even if the child responds to some environmental sounds.

rows: Lack of stimulation or developmental delay
Knowledge of motor skills affected by neurological disease

items.text: Most children walk independently by 18 months.

blocks.text: Red flag: Failure to walk independently by 18 months warrants developmental assessment.
Exam pearl: Delayed walking accompanied by regression, abnormal tone, muscle weakness or loss of reflexes requires urgent evaluation.
Primitive reflexes are automatic neurological responses present during early infancy that gradually integrate as the nervous system matures.
This is a recall aid; the most important clinical task is knowing how to elicit each reflex and its expected integration age.
Exam pearl: The Babinski response is normally extensor in infants and may persist into the second year of life.
Growth charts are graphical tools used to monitor a child's physical growth over time.

rows: Height, weight and BMI interpreted by age and sex

items.text: Recumbent length: Generally used below 2 years.
Standing height: Generally used from 2 years onwards.
Reflects skull and brain growth, particularly in infancy.
Measured around the largest occipitofrontal circumference.

blocks.text: Interpreted using age- and sex-specific growth charts in children.

rows: Severe undernutrition or severe growth deficit, depending on index
High value requiring interpretation according to the index

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Always interpret growth measurements against the correct age- and sex-specific chart, using corrected age where appropriate for premature infants.

rows: Sensory assessment, including hearing and vision

items.text: Obtain antenatal, birth and neonatal history.
Identify any loss of acquired skills.
Examine tone, reflexes, hearing and vision.
Arrange investigations and specialist referral where indicated.
Chronological age: Actual age since birth.
Corrected age: Chronological age minus the number of weeks born before 40 weeks' gestation.
Developmental quotient (DQ): Developmental age divided by chronological age × 100.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Screening tools identify children who may need further assessment; they do not independently establish a definitive developmental diagnosis.
Immunisation protects children against vaccine-preventable diseases and is one of the most important interventions in preventive paediatrics.

rows: BCG, OPV0, Hepatitis B birth dose
Pentavalent 1, OPV1, PCV1, Rotavirus 1, IPV according to current schedule
Additional vaccines according to the current national schedule, including malaria vaccine in eligible implementation areas
Measles-containing vaccine, yellow fever and other nationally scheduled vaccines
Second measles-containing dose where included in the current schedule
Additional measles-containing dose where included in the current schedule

blocks.text: Important: Nigeria's immunisation programme has undergone updates, including introduction of newer vaccines and changes to dose timing. The exact national schedule and state-level implementation should be checked against the latest NPHCDA immunisation card and guidance before clinical use.
BCG – OPV – PENTA – PCV – ROTA – IPV – MEASLES – YELLOW FEVER

rows: Diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Hib

items.text: Severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or vaccine component: contraindication to that vaccine.
Severe immunodeficiency: contraindication to certain live vaccines.
Moderate or severe acute illness: may require postponement.
Mild illness and low-grade fever are generally not contraindications.
Premature infants generally follow chronological-age vaccination schedules, with special considerations for hepatitis B birth dosing in some circumstances.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: A child who misses a vaccine dose generally does not need to restart the entire vaccination series. Continue using an appropriate catch-up schedule.
Children have different nutritional requirements depending on age, growth rate, activity and health status.

items.text: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months.
Breast milk supplies energy, nutrients and immune protection.
Vitamin D supplementation may be indicated according to local guidance and infant circumstances.
No routine water or other foods are needed in healthy term infants receiving exclusive breastfeeding.
Start complementary feeding at around 6 months.
Start with small amounts and increase gradually.
Continue breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond.
Ensure adequate protein, iron, calcium and essential fats.
G – Greater energy requirements during growth spurts.
R – Require increased iron, especially menstruating adolescents.
O – Optimal calcium and vitamin D for bone health.
W – Well-balanced protein, carbohydrates and fats.

rows: DNA synthesis and red cell production
Neurological function and red cell production

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Complementary feeding begins at approximately 6 months because breast milk alone becomes insufficient to meet all nutritional requirements, particularly iron and energy needs.
